text:
tess: quick thread — following the soft-cancel convo we had, i want to nail down how gateway signs/validates resume tokens and how that interacts with tls termination/sidecars.

jia: good call. our earlier notes assumed opaque resume tokens but didn't specify authenticity. we should HMAC them with a per-cluster key so gateways can validate tokens without hitting control plane.

sam: +1. HMAC gives us cheap validation. do we include sequence numbers inside the token or just point to upstream checkpoint id?

tess: include both: token payload = base64(json{checkpoint_id, seq, route_fingerprint, expiry}) then signed. keeps resume logic deterministic and lets us detect rewind attacks.

anya: how big will tokens be? SDKs will carry them as trailers, must be reasonably small. maybe compress/shorten checkpoint ids server-side to 16 bytes.

jia: agreed — canonical checkpoint is 128-bit hex; seq is 32-bit. signature 32 bytes. overall under ~120 bytes which is fine for trailers.

envoy-bot: note: when terminating TLS at edge, ensure we don't leak HMAC keys to sidecars. recommend split key material: per-region signing key in gateway, per-cluster rotate every 24h.

sam: rotation semantics matter. we need to support validating tokens signed with the previous key for a short TTL to avoid invalidating in-flight resumes. add key id header in token: kid.

tess: good point. token shape example (pseudo):
```
RW-Resume-Token: eyJraWQiOiJrZXkxIiwic2VxIjoxMjMsImNoZWNrcG9pbnQiOiJhYmNkIn0=.sig
```
where kid is included in payload.

jia: next up: what do we do when upstream never hands a checkpoint? i propose gateway synthesizes ephemeral checkpoints by hashing the emitted prefix + route_fingerprint. i know it's imperfect but gives resume-on-replay a chance.

anya: hmm that risks nondeterminism if upstream internal state diverges. we should mark those as `weak_checkpoint` in the token and only allow resume for idempotent paths. no hedging if weak_checkpoint.

sam: agree. policy table: strong_checkpoint => allow hedged retry and resume; weak_checkpoint => allow client-initiated resume only if route marked idempotent; no_checkpoint => no resume, return INCOMPLETE error.

tess: SDK surface: when we return INCOMPLETE we should include `resume_hint: null` and `billing_tokens_charged` so clients can decide to restart. keep response enums stable.

ops-bot: rollout scheduled: `resume-token-signing` feature-flag enabled for 10% canary.

jia: observability: emit span attributes `rw.resume.kid`, `rw.checkpoint.type` and counters for `resume_attempts`, `resume_success`, `resume_fallback_to_rerun`. should make postmortems easier.

anya: on billing: partial payouts earned at the moment we emit `partial_done` trailer. need a hook in billing pipeline to accept interim-usage events keyed by request_id + resume_token_kid. otherwise we risk double-billing on replay.

sam: ergo, billing pipeline must dedupe by `(request_fingerprint, resume_token_signature)` for a TTL equal to token expiry. we'll add a dedicated `billing_dedup` table.

jia: final thought: grpc streaming vs http chunked differences — for grpc we can put resume token in trailing metadata; for chunked http use trailers. SDKs should abstract this away. add compatibility tests in SDK matrix.

tess: action items: (1) write token spec + examples, (2) add key-rotation plan + TTLs, (3) update model manifest schema with `supports_resume: strong|weak|none`, (4) add tests for weak_checkpoint behavior, (5) billing dedupe PR. i'll own 1–3.

anya: i'll own billing dedupe and telemetry hooks.

sam: i'll add SDK compatibility tests and raise a small infra ticket for key storage.

envoy-bot: note: suggested minimal envoy filter change posted: https://git.internal/envoy/patch/1234

ops-bot: ci: `resume-token-signing-canary` green on canary 10% :party_popper:

tess: nice. i'll draft RFC appendix updates and ping arch for review.
